title: One Energy Enterprises Inc. et al. v. Board of Allen Township Trustees of Hancock County

case.caption: One Energy Enterprises Inc. et al. v. Board of Allen Township Trustees of Hancock County
case.court: Court of Appeals of Ohio, Third Appellate District, Hancock County
case.trial_court: Hancock County Court of Common Pleas
case.author: Waldick, J.

counsel.appellants: Marion H. Little, Jr. (for One Energy, appellants/cross-appellees)
counsel.appellee: Teresa L. Grigsby (for the Board, appellee/cross-appellant)

case.costs: assessed to Appellant; causes remanded to the trial court for execution of the judgment for costs

plaintiffs_appellants.name: One Energy Enterprises, Inc.
plaintiffs_appellants.detail: [verified] fn.3 — "a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business in Hancock County, Ohio."

plaintiffs_appellants.name: unnamed additional plaintiffs
plaintiffs_appellants.detail: [open] fn.1 describes them only as "entities that have land interests in Allen Township" and names none. Identifying them is a retrieval target — they are the landowning side of the One Energy position in the township.

defendant_appellee.name: Board of Allen Township Trustees of Hancock County
defendant_appellee.detail: [verified] fn.2 — "comprised of three trustees and a fiscal officer."

chronology.event: One Energy petitioned the Hancock County Commissioners to rename Township Road 215 "Electric Avenue." Without convening a public meeting, the Board decided to attend the Commissioners' daytime meeting and oppose the renaming. At its own regular meeting that evening, residents raised zoning as a way to regulate wind-turbine expansion; counsel explained the R.C. 519.04 steps. After the meeting adjourned, some members stayed to discuss who might serve on a zoning commission and what traits were desirable.
Notice published in the Findlay Courier of a December 20 special meeting listing "two resolutions (zoning and marijuana)."
At the special meeting the Board moved to proceed with zoning and to establish a zoning commission under R.C. 519.04. Both resolutions passed without discussion; public comment was not solicited.
One Energy filed case 2024 CV 00038 seeking declaratory relief for Open Meetings Act violations.

The Board adopted a revised notice policy (fearing the original rule was lost or destroyed) and RESCINDED both December 20 zoning resolutions. Minutes reflect the township attorney recommending that residents be required to petition for zoning.
Hancock County Board of Elections certified the resident petitions.
Nine petitions bearing 141 signatures were presented, asking the Board to move to place zoning for the unincorporated areas on the ballot. The Board instructed the attorney to prepare a resolution.
A protest was filed against the Board of Elections' certification placing zoning on the November ballot.

After an eight-minute executive session on pending litigation, the Board proceeded with zoning BY ITS OWN RESOLUTION rather than on the petitions, and passed a second resolution establishing a new zoning commission. The new commission's members gathered afterward; One Energy's president/CEO claimed his filming was thwarted.

One Energy filed a second complaint (the opinion writes "2024-CR-161" here; the caption page says 2024 CV 00161) alleging the Board failed to deliberate in public over who would sit on the zoning commission and by what criteria.
Trial. One Energy expressly disclaimed statutory damages, attorney's fees and costs, seeking only compliance, declarations, and invalidation of the April 2024 zoning commission.
Final judgment entries in both cases.

violations_found:
Taking an official position opposing the renaming of Township Road 215 without discussing it in an open meeting violated R.C. 121.22. The chairman testified he discussed the position by phone with the other members and then stated "the Board's position" at the Commissioners' meeting (¶29). Pleading objection rejected: Ohio is a notice-pleading state and the issue was fully litigated (¶27).
Remaining after the December 5, 2023 meeting to discuss criteria for selecting zoning commission members was a deliberation, not fact-finding, and violated the Act (¶¶33-34).
claims_rejected: Notice of the December 20, 2023 special meeting was sufficient.
The December 5, 2023 minutes were prepared in a timely manner.
The April 2, 2024 executive session was properly invoked to discuss the One Energy litigation.
The evidence did not establish that the decision to proceed with zoning resulted from nonpublic deliberations.

remedy.granted: A prospective injunction: the trustees "are prospectively enjoined from engaging in private discussions of public matters in derogation of R.C. §121.22." Mandatory under R.C. 121.22(I)(1) once a violation is proven, though the trial court retains discretion over its terms (¶¶35, 40).
remedy.refused: The court declined to strike the selection criteria or invalidate the April 2024 zoning commission, on the trial court's three stated grounds: the informal discussion produced no official action subject to invalidation; the rescission of the December 2023 resolutions "constitutes an intervening circumstances that breaks any causal link"; and the criteria "were not unique" — "This Court declines to enjoin the use of common sense" (¶40).

holdings.bottom_line: [verified] Both sides lost every assignment of error. The zoning-commission actions of April 2, 2024 STAND. The Open Meetings Act violations are real and declared, but they did not undo the zoning track — which is why the instrument that eventually reached the electorate traces to the April 2024 resolution and not to the rescinded December 2023 one.

key_authority: Look Ahead Am. v. Stark Cnty. Bd. of Elections, 2024-Ohio-2691, ¶15 — OMA interpretation is de novo
State ex rel. Pelmear v. Henry Cnty. Land Reutilization Corp., 2025-Ohio-4998, ¶24, ¶30
Ames v. Rootstown Twp. Bd. of Trustees, 2022-Ohio-4605, ¶¶20-21 — injunction mandatory, terms discretionary
State ex rel. Bratenahl v. Village of Bratenahl, 2019-Ohio-3233, ¶23 — rescission does not moot a proven violation
Springfield Local Sch. Dist. Bd. of Educ. v. Ohio Assn. of Pub. Sch. Emps., Local 530, 106 Ohio App.3d 855 (9th Dist.) — causation required beyond the act of deliberation
Blakemore v. Blakemore, 5 Ohio St.3d 217, 219 (1983) — abuse-of-discretion standard

corroboration.claim: The Wind-for-Industry turbines serve industrial hosts, not the Megawatt Hub.
corroboration.detail: ¶2 of the opinion states as the court's own background that One Energy "was making plans to construct additional wind turbines in Allen Township to, inter alia, provide power to the Whirlpool manufacturing facility." Independently corroborates the correction recorded in issue 1464 (see data/extracted/grid/findlay/) that nothing places generation at the Megawatt Hub, from a source that is neither a company filing nor press.

corroboration.claim: The zoning fight was triggered by WIND, and data centers were nowhere in it.
corroboration.detail: The opinion's entire factual account — turbines, a road renaming, a zoning commission — runs from late 2023 through December 2024 without a single reference to data centers or computing load. The data-center question arrives in Allen Township only in 2026, after the resolution is already adopted and awaiting a referendum. That sequencing is why the adopted resolution has no data-center provision to be found: it was not drafted against that use.

fields.title: Allen Township proposed Section 1521 — DATA CENTERS, and the Section 1520 replacement (ATZC Resolutions 24-04-124M / 24-04-125M, heard 2026-08-19)
fields.authority: R.C. 519.12 — amendment initiated by resolution of the zoning commission

resolutions.subject: adds a new Section 1521 — DATA CENTERS, plus definitions into Section 201
resolutions.hearing: 2026-08-19 at 7:30 p.m., Allen Township Center, 12829 St. Rt. 613, Van Buren
resolutions.note: Attachment A's own "Resolution No. ____" line is left BLANK; the number appears only on the two resolution pages. Handwritten throughout.

resolutions.subject: REPLACES Section 1520 (Energy Storage Related to Wind and Solar Facilities) with a technology-neutral Section 1520 — Energy Storage Systems
resolutions.note: [inference] The replacement matters independently of its limits: the ADOPTED Sec. 1520 only reaches storage "related to wind and solar facilities," so storage sited to firm a large computing load arguably fell outside it altogether. The amendment closes that by dropping the wind/solar tether.

resolutions.subject: clerical corrections — moves Zoning Commission duties to the Board of Zoning Appeals, renumbers the duplicated Section 1201, adds pools in A-1
resolutions.note: Its resolution PDF was not captured (only the notice page). ⚠️ It is not cosmetic and it is not severable from the data-center amendment — see `interlock` below.

proposed_section_1521.mechanism: Conditional use only. "No person shall cause, allow or maintain the use of a Data Center or Data Center Campus without first having obtained a conditional zoning permit from Zoning Inspector after approval by the Board of Zoning Appeals in accordance with section 1802."

cooling.permitted_verbatim: All data centers shall be air cooled (dry cooling).

water.groundwater_verbatim: No regulated use shall utilize groundwater wells, private wells, or other subsurface water sources for operational or cooling purposes.
permitted_sources: a municipal water and sewer system
water.verification_required: written verification from the water utility provider demonstrating adequate system capacity to serve the proposed use without negatively impacting existing users

electrical.phased_development_verbatim: Developments constructed in phases shall be considered a single site if: Located on contiguous parcels; or Sharing electrical infrastructure, substations, or utility interconnections. The combined load of all phases shall not exceed the 10 MW limit.

nuisance_standards.vibration_odor_heat: No vibration, odor, or heat perceptible beyond the property line.
nuisance_standards.emergency_generators: May operate for testing and maintenance between 8 a.m. - 6 p.m. weekdays only, except during power outages.

proposed_section_1521.anti_circumvention_verbatim: The Zoning Administrator requires submission of ownership, lease, and utility agreements to determine common control. No data center development shall be artificially divided into multiple parcels, entities, or applications for the purpose of avoiding the requirements of this section.

definitions_verbatim.data_center: A facility designed and used primarily for housing computer servers, data storage, networking, or related equipment for the purpose of storing, processing, or distributing electronic data. Data centers shall not be considered warehouses, storage facilities, or distribution centers for zoning purposes. Such facilities may include ancillary offices for employees, network operations, and limited support functions, but shall not include general office space, call centers, or telecommunications towers as the principal use.
definitions_verbatim.data_center_campus: A group of data center buildings and associated infrastructure located on one or more adjacent parcels under common ownership or control and functioning as an integrated development.
definitions_verbatim.warehousing: The business operation, or institution of the storing of goods, or merchandise.

drafting_record.event: Four weeks before the referendum, Timmerman asked counsel whether the proposed resolution would permit a data center. "Cindy stated that a data center would not be permitted." (Lucinda Land, Assistant Hancock County Prosecutor.)

Three weeks after the resolution took effect, Land "recommended that language be drafted for the zoning resolution to state the location, requirements and conditions regarding data centers and battery energy storage systems, BESS."

Stacy circulated data-center language "written by Hancock County Regional Planning on behalf of Washington Township"; Timmerman circulated his own draft "that followed a pattern similar to the wind and solar sections in our adopted zoning resolution book." A special drafting meeting was set.

The drafting session. Timmerman "merged information from Washington Township's language ... and the information that John compiled and wrote on behalf of Allen Township"; "Definitions included in Washington Township's language will become a part of Allen Township's language." The ESS draft was NOT finished — "more time was needed to gather information" — yet both topics were carried into the August 19 hearing.

Justin Kahl, Hancock County Assistant Prosecutor
drafting_record.note: [verified] that these four attended and are so described in the minutes. ⚠️ The minutes give no affiliation detail beyond these strings, and this repo does NOT here assert who any guest was there for. title: Maumee Watershed Nutrient TMDL — Findlay WPCF total-phosphorus wasteload allocation
warnings: The 3.2 metric tons (Table A4.1) and the 3,200 kg (OHP000001 Part IV.A.1) are the SAME allocation stated in two units by two instruments, not two allocations. Do not add them.

Table A4.5's seven numeric columns are, in order, 2008 / WLA / 2017 / 2018 / 2019 / 2020 / 2021. The first column is a 2008 baseline load and the second is the allocation — reading the row left-to-right as a time series would misreport both.

The most recent per-facility spring load on this record is 2021. The 2024 Biennial Report publishes only the BASIN GROUP total, not Findlay's own load, so no post-2021 Findlay figure is asserted here. Whether Findlay is still over its allocation is [open] — the annual Season Report required by OHP000001 Part IV.D is the record that would answer it (a records-request lead).

fields.note: [verified] Findlay WPCF's spring-season total-phosphorus wasteload allocation is 3.2 metric tons (3,200 kg), and its reported spring loads for every year on the TMDL's own record — 2017 through 2021 — were 4.8, 5.5, 5.3, 5.5 and 5.4 metric tons. Its 2008 baseline load, 4.4 MT, was also above it. The allocation is enforced not through the plant's individual permit but through the Maumee Watershed Total Phosphorus general permit OHP000001, whose compliance rule (Part IV.C.3) makes an individual exceedance a violation ONLY when the 39-facility CUMULATIVE load also exceeds its cap. In the 2024 spring season the group reported 43,304 kg against a 64,170 kg cap — 20,866 kg of headroom — so an over-allocation Findlay load was not, on that record, a violation of anything.

title: AEP Ohio's Rocky Ford 138 kV Station + the Ebersole-Fostoria Central #2 cut-in and Rocky Ford-Border Basin tie line — Cass Township, Hancock County, Ohio

meta.subject: AEP Ohio's Rocky Ford 138 kV Station + the Ebersole-Fostoria Central #2 cut-in and Rocky Ford-Border Basin tie line — Cass Township, Hancock County, Ohio
meta.method: Direct read of the two OPSB filings' own PDF text layers plus AEP's public notice for the same pair. Both case numbers are printed on the filings themselves; nothing here is taken from a docket search or from press.

primary.file: data/documents/grid/findlay/Rocky Ford 138 kV Station Project Letter of Notification.pdf
data/documents/grid/findlay/Ebersole-Fostoria Center 2 138 kV Cut-In and Rocky Ford-Border Basin 138 kV Tie Line Project Construction Notice.pdf
data/documents/grid/findlay/Rocky Ford 138 kV Station Project Public Notice.pdf

opsb_cases.statement: The project is TWO OPSB cases, filed the same day for the same point of interconnection, because Ohio's application-requirement matrix splits them. Both numbers are printed on the filings' own cover pages and repeated in AEP's public notice.

cases.applicant: AEP Ohio Transmission Company, Inc. ("AEP Ohio Transco")
cases.covers: Construction of the Rocky Ford 138 kV Station (~6.25 acres). Qualifies as an LON under item (3) of Appendix A to O.A.C. 4906-1-01 — "Constructing a new electric power transmission substation."
cases.source: Letter of Notification cover page + B(1), p. 1

cases.covers: The Ebersole-Fostoria Central #2 138 kV cut-in and the Rocky Ford-Border Basin 138 kV tie line. Qualifies as a CN under item (1)(a) of the same appendix (new construction/extension of transmission circuits).
cases.source: Construction Notice cover page + B(1), p. 1

opsb_cases.note: Two different applicants — the transmission-only affiliate files the station, the operating company files the lines. Do not collapse them into one filer.

location.landmark: "near the intersection of Township Road 238 and County Road 216" (public notice); topographic quadrangles Arcadia, OH and Bloomdale, OH
location.source: LON B(3) p. 2 + B(10)(a) p. 4; CN B(8) p. 4; public notice p. 1

lines.cut_in: Loop the existing Fostoria-East Lima 138 kV transmission line (specifically the Ebersole-Fostoria Central #2 138 kV circuit) through Rocky Ford Station by extending two single-circuit 138 kV lines of less than 0.1 mile each.
lines.tie: One span of 138 kV line, approximately 0.04 mile, from Rocky Ford Station to a Point of Interconnection with the IPP's own 138 kV transmission line.
lines.conductor: 795 KCM 26/7 ACSR Drake; 100 ft ROW; galvanized steel poles on drilled-pier foundations
lines.public_notice_summary: "less than 0.2 miles of 138-kilovolt (kV) transmission line connecting Rocky Ford Station to a customer facility and an existing 138-kV transmission line"
lines.source: CN B(1) p. 1, B(2) p. 2, B(9)(a) p. 4; public notice p. 1

schedule.source: LON B(6) p. 3; CN B(6) p. 3

status_as_captured.statement: Whether the station and lines actually energized on the December 2025 schedule is not established by any captured source. AEP's filings state a PLAN; no in-service confirmation, PJM notice, or OPSB compliance filing was captured. Do not write "in service" without one.

cost.cost_recovery: Both filings say the same thing in the same words: "The costs for this Project will be recovered through total reimbursement by the IPP." Neither project is a ratepayer-funded network upgrade — the generator pays.
cost.source: LON B(9)(c) p. 4; CN B(9)(c) p. 5

correction_to_issue_body.statement: Issue 1464 carried "~$2.2M" as the cost of "Rocky Ford 138 kV Station + Rocky Ford-Border Basin tie." The $2,214,000 is the LINE project (24-0706-EL-BNR) alone; the station (24-0707-EL-BLN) is a separate $8,700,000. Combined, the pair is ~$10.9M, all IPP-reimbursed.

purpose.statement: Both filings state the identical need: "The Border Basin I IPP plans to build a 120 MW Maximum Facility Output (81 MW Capacity) solar generating facility near Arcadia, Ohio. As part of the AE1-146 IPP Interconnection Service Agreement, the Company will be required to connect the proposed facilities to the electric grid." Failure to proceed would jeopardize "the customer's required in-service date per the FERC approved Interconnection Service Agreement."
purpose.interconnecting_customer: Border Basin I, LLC — an Independent Power Producer
purpose.in_aep_long_term_forecast: 2024 Long Term Forecast Report, pp. 109-110 (reproduced at LON Appendix B)

what_this_is_not.statement: AE1-146 is a GENERATOR's queue position — Border Basin I's solar plant — and Rocky Ford is the substation built to receive it. It is NOT a large-load interconnection, NOT a data-center service point, and NOT the One Power "Findlay Megawatt Hub" +300 MW standalone interconnection this epic is looking for. The two sit in different townships (Cass, near Arcadia, versus the Hub's Allen Township) and answer to different processes: a FERC-jurisdictional generator interconnection agreement versus a retail electric service agreement under AEP Ohio's Schedule DCT. The "customer facility" in AEP's public notice is Border Basin I's own station. Anyone reading the county's grid record must not let the presence of a fresh 138 kV substation stand in for the load instrument that is still missing — see megawatt-hub-interconnection.gap.yaml.

review.agricultural_district: Both project areas sit on a parcel enrolled in Ohio's Agricultural District Land program, verified with the Hancock County Auditor's Office on 2024-08-20; the parcel "will not be eligible and will be withdrawn from the program by the Company." Station ~6.25 acres, lines ~1.5 acres.
review.land_use: Hancock County Auditor land use "Other Agricultural Use with Outbuildings Qualified for Current Use Value"; field observation found the area entirely agricultural field. No tree clearing anticipated.
review.cultural_resources: Phase I archaeological and history/architectural surveys conducted January 2024. One new archaeological site identified, not recommended NRHP-eligible; six resources fifty years or older in the APE, none recommended eligible. SHPO correspondence received 2024-02-12 agreeing the Project will have no effect on historic properties and that no further coordination is necessary.
review.proximity: No occupied residence or institution within 100 feet (so the EMF section is stated inapplicable); no cemetery, church, school or community facility within 1,000 feet.

central_findlay_project.statement: Issue 1464 asked for the "Central Findlay Improvement Project" OPSB LON case number. There is no OPSB case to find, and the reason is jurisdictional, not a search failure. AEP Ohio's own description of the work is 69 kV — "Rebuilding four miles of 69-kilovolt (kV) transmission line, installing two miles of overhead 69-kV transmission line and installing one mile of underground 69-kV transmission line" — and Ohio's siting jurisdiction begins at 100 kV. R.C. 4906.01(B)(2) defines a "major utility facility" to include an "electric transmission line and associated facilities of a design capacity of one hundred kilovolts or more," and the O.A.C. 4906-1-01 Appendix A application matrix that produced the two Rocky Ford filings applies to that same class. A 69 kV rebuild is below the threshold, so it generates neither an LON nor a CN. AEP's Ohio regulatory-filings index carries no Central Findlay entry, consistent with that.
central_findlay_project.scope_correction: The issue body described it as "~4 mi rebuild, ~1 mi underground." AEP's own text is three components — 4 mi rebuilt + 2 mi new overhead + 1 mi new underground, all at 69 kV, not 138 kV.
central_findlay_project.stated_purpose: "These improvements support the area's electrical needs and strengthen the local power grid by replacing aging equipment." No customer, load, or data-center connection is stated.

residual_open.statement: The project factsheet URL the issue carried is 404 and AEP's page gives no schedule, cost, or route. A 69 kV rebuild still needs local road/ROW permissions and would appear in AEP Ohio's distribution capital filings at PUCO, so the record is thin rather than closed. Lead CENTRAL-FINDLAY-69KV.

solar_export_load_import.statement: Border Basin I is one of the two utility-scale solar projects Hancock County's 2022 S.B. 52 restricted-area designation grandfathered (the other is South Branch). Rocky Ford is the transmission instrument that builds one of those two out. Read against the load side of this county's record — a 150 MW contracted compute load already operating at the One Power hub and an undocumented +300 MW of "available" capacity beyond it — the county is wiring out 81 MW of solar capacity while its large-load question stays unanswered. The two facts are verified; the framing that joins them is reasoning, and the S.B. 52 designation itself belongs to the governance sub-issue, not this record.
solar_export_load_import.source: LON B(2) p. 1 (Border Basin 120 MW MFO / 81 MW capacity); the S.B. 52 restricted-area designation is carried in issue 1464's research refresh and is NOT independently captured here — do not cite this record for it.

no_new_profile_field.statement: As with the Lima "Lyka" record (issue 1476), no SiteProfile/SiteFacility schema field is added for a transmission-siting project. `GridProfile` (src/watermark/grid/model.py) is the connector-generated quantitative backdrop — serving utility, EIA-861 utility profile, EIA-930 BA load, and the campus load share — with `extra="forbid"`; a siting docket, a tariff posture, and a behind-the-meter fleet are corpus instruments, not denominators, and inlining them would put hand-curated prose inside a file the next connector run rewrites. They live here instead, and `_FINDLAY.serving_utility_citation` (the one hand-authored input that reaches grid-profile.yaml) points at them.

source_doc_rel: grid/findlay/Rocky Ford 138 kV Station Project Letter of Notification.pdf

title: AEP Ohio Schedule DCT (Data Center Tariff), P.U.C.O. No. 22 Original Sheet Nos. 223-1 to 223-7 — the terms as filed, and which of them bite at the One Power "Findlay Megawatt Hub"

meta.subject: AEP Ohio Schedule DCT (Data Center Tariff), P.U.C.O. No. 22 Original Sheet Nos. 223-1 to 223-7 — the terms as filed, and which of them bite at the One Power "Findlay Megawatt Hub"
meta.method: Verbatim read of the tariff sheets in Ohio Power Company's own filed tariff book. Every quoted term below is from the sheets, not from a press summary or a law-firm client alert. Procedural history and the appeal are sourced separately and tagged accordingly.

procedural_history.statement: AEP Ohio filed its Application for Approval of New Tariffs on 2024-05-13 in PUCO Case No. 24-508-EL-ATA. The Commission issued its order adopting a settlement on 2025-07-09 (signatories reported as AEP Ohio, PUCO Staff, the Office of the Ohio Consumers' Counsel, the Ohio Energy Group, Walmart and Ohio Partners for Affordable Energy), ordering AEP Ohio to file updated tariffs and to "lift its moratorium on connecting new data centers as soon as possible." The compliance tariff followed on 2025-07-11 and took effect 2025-07-23.
procedural_history.why_reference_not_verified: The Commission's Opinion and Order itself is NOT in the corpus. PUCO's Docketing Information System (dis.puc.state.oh.us) rejects automated retrieval — both the case record and a direct ViewImage document request returned an application-firewall "Request Rejected" page on 2026-07-31 — and PUCO's own news page for this order now 404s, leaving a GovDelivery mirror. So the dates and settlement roster above rest on secondary text. The TARIFF TERMS below do not: those are read off the filed sheets.

the_tariff_dates_itself.statement: The sheets close the loop on their own origin. Sheet 223-2 defines "'Effective Date of Schedule DCT' means the date Schedule DCT became effective following the Commission's order in Case No. 24-508-EL-ATA."

currently_filed_version.statement: The sheets captured here are stamped "Filed pursuant to Order dated April 1, 2026 in Case No. 25-392-EL-AIR / Issued: April 8, 2026 / Effective: April 10, 2026" — the schedule as re-issued in AEP Ohio's distribution rate case, not the July 2025 compliance sheet. The tariff book compilation itself is dated 2026-07-24. Any comparison against the 2025 original is [open]; the original compliance sheet is not captured.
currently_filed_version.source: tariff book, Original Sheet Nos. 223-1..223-7 and Sheet No. 101-1

on_appeal.statement: The order is on appeal to the Supreme Court of Ohio, Case No. 2025-1458, "In the Matter of the Application of Ohio Power Company for New Tariffs Related to Data Centers and Mobile Data Centers," on appeal from Pub. Util. Comm. Case No. 24-508-EL-ATA. Appellant is The Ohio Manufacturers' Association Energy Group (counsel Kimberly W. Bojko, Carpenter Lipps LLP); the PUCO is appellee and the Office of the Ohio Consumers' Counsel filed a merit brief as intervening appellee on 2026-03-24. OMA's propositions of law run to undue discrimination / equal protection, sufficiency of the evidence, and the specificity of the Commission's reasoning under R.C. 4903.09, plus a contention that the case was an application for an increase in rates under R.C. 4909.18.

disposition.statement: No decision was located as of 2026-07-31. The tariff is in force pending appeal. Do not write that the tariff has been upheld or vacated.

on_appeal.source: Merit Brief of Intervening Appellee, Office of the Ohio Consumers' Counsel, Ohio S.Ct. No. 2025-1458, filed 2026-03-24 (read at supremecourt.ohio.gov; caption + tables of contents; not committed to the corpus)

terms.source: tariff book, Original Sheet Nos. 223-1 through 223-7

who_it_applies_to.data_center_definition: "a centralized facility (a) used primarily or exclusively for electronic information services such as the management, storage, processing, and dissemination of electronic data and information through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components that (b) has an aggregate monthly maximum demand of greater than 25,000 kW. Unless otherwise specified, the term 'Data Center' shall include 'Mobile Data Center.'"
who_it_applies_to.mobile_data_center_definition: the same, but "(including mining of cryptocurrency)" and "has load that is portable and/or distributable, including but not limited to structures that are not affixed to the ground or are easily removed from a location."
who_it_applies_to.availability: Service is available to customers operating a Data Center that will use, within the initial contract term, a monthly maximum demand greater than 25,000 kW "at a Single Location or an aggregated Total Customer Contract Capacity in Service Territory of greater than 25,000 kW." Mixed sites are swept in whole unless the customer separately meters at its own cost.

existing_vs_new_load.existing_load: "Data Center load for which a letter of agreement or electric service agreement has already been signed by the Effective Date of Schedule DCT." It "does not include Data Center load for which a customer signs a new electric service agreement to expand its Existing Load by more than 25,000 kW of New Load above the contract capacity under the existing electric service agreement after the Effective Date." Un-separately-metered expansions cost the whole load its Existing Load status.
existing_vs_new_load.new_load: "(a) Data Center load for which a letter of agreement or electric service agreement was signed after the Effective Date of Schedule DCT or (b) Existing Load that signs a new ESA to increase its contract capacity by more than 25,000 kW." Expansions of 25,000 kW or less do not convert.

minimum_billing_demand.existing_load: Not less than 60% of the contract capacity or of the highest previously established monthly billing demand in the past 11 months.
minimum_billing_demand.new_load_during_ramp: Not less than 85% of the customer's Load Ramp Contract Capacity, where the Load Ramp Contract Capacity is itself floored at 50% / 65% / 80% / 90% of Contract Capacity in Years 1 / 2 / 3 / 4.
minimum_billing_demand.new_load_after_ramp: Not less than the greater of (a) 85% of the highest previously established monthly billing demand in the past 11 months, or (b) the "Minimum Demand" table — 15,000 kW plus 85% of the marginal amount over 25,000 kW for a total contract capacity of 25,001-75,000 kW; 57,500 kW plus 100% of the marginal amount over 75,000 kW above that, capped at 85% of total contract capacity.
minimum_billing_demand.aggregation: "All New Loads of affiliated companies and companies with common ownership greater than 25,000 kW will be considered in the aggregate" for the Total Customer Contract Capacity, stacked by energization date. Existing Load is excluded from that aggregate.
minimum_billing_demand.reconciliation_note: This is where the widely repeated shorthand "data centers must pay for 85% of contracted capacity" comes from, and it is close enough to be usable but not precise enough to quote. The 85% is a floor applied to a RAMPED capacity during the ramp and to a rolling 11-month peak (or the Minimum Demand table) afterwards. The Year-4 ramp floor is 90%, which is higher than 85% — the two numbers are not in conflict because they multiply different things. Cite the sheets, not the shorthand.

contract_term.new_load: "contracts under the Schedule shall be made for an initial period of not less than the Load Ramp Period plus 8 years. By way of example, the initial period of a Contract for a Data Center with a 4-year Load Ramp Period will be 12 years." After the initial term either party needs three years' written notice to terminate or to change Contract Capacity.
contract_term.existing_load: Existing contracts run on their own terms until terminated under those terms; the Company is not required to supply capacity above Contract Capacity except by mutual agreement.
contract_term.exit_fee: "If after completion of the fifth year of the Contract after the Load Ramp Period the customer chooses to pay an exit fee equal to minimum charges for 36 months after notice of termination, the customer can thereafter terminate the contract."
contract_term.load_additions: A new contract is required for any load addition in excess of 100 kW.
contract_term.site_control: "the customer must designate a specific site at which its Data Center project will be constructed and served by the Company, and the customer must own or have the exclusive right to use the land for this purpose."

collateral.new_load: Unless the customer holds both an A-/A3 credit rating and liquidity above ten times the requirement, it must post a guarantee, standby letter of credit, or cash equal to 50% of the total minimum charges for the full contract term, reduced by one year's minimum charges for each year energized with on-time payment.

behind_the_meter_generation.interconnection_agreement: "Consistent with Ohio Administrative Code Chapter 4901:1-22, Schedule DCT Customers shall enter into an interconnection agreement between the Company and the Customer in advance of connecting any source of power other than the delivery point specified in the Contract. Emergency or backup generation that is not designed to operate in parallel with the Company's system is not subject to the additional requirements in this section."
behind_the_meter_generation.netting_election: A customer electing to use behind-the-meter generation to OFFSET its Contract Capacity must keep equipment in place "to instantaneously curtail load equal to or greater than the behind-the-meter generation output." A customer that does NOT elect to net may have service suspended, with Commission approval, if usage exceeds Contract Capacity by more than 1,000 kW.

terms.mobile_data_center_attestation: "Prior to receiving service, Mobile Data Center customers will be required to provide a sworn statement, under penalty of perjury, that neither the customer nor its corporate parent or affiliates are affiliated with or acting on behalf of any foreign adversary as defined in 15 C.F.R. § 7.4," with an immediate disconnection right on a good-faith belief of falsity.
terms.transmission_voltage_charges: Schedule codes 297/797 (transmission service voltage): customer charge $6,800/month plus a supplemental customer charge of $20,000/month, the latter expressly "not a base distribution rate ... and will not apply to Existing Load"; excess reactive demand $0.95/kVAR beyond 50% of metered kW.

scale_test.statement: MARA Holdings' contracted 150 MW at the One Power Findlay Megawatt Hub is 150,000 kW — six times the 25,000 kW threshold — and the 30 MW currently energized already clears it. Whatever else is unresolved, this is not a site that falls below Schedule DCT on size.
scale_test.source: One Power Co Form S-1 (EDGAR CIK 2039139, filed 2025-01-23) + the tariff's 25,000 kW definition; see data/extracted/findlay/data-centers.md

crypto_is_named_in_the_tariff.statement: The tariff does not leave cryptocurrency mining to interpretation. "Mobile Data Center" is defined to reach electronic information services "(including mining of cryptocurrency)" with portable or distributable load, and "Data Center" is defined to include "Mobile Data Center" unless stated otherwise. MARA Holdings, Inc. is a bitcoin miner. A Findlay compute load of that description, taken as a retail customer of AEP Ohio above 25,000 kW, is squarely inside the definition — and it inherits the sworn foreign-adversary attestation, which is the only place in this tariff where a customer must swear to anything.
crypto_is_named_in_the_tariff.guard: MARA Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ MARA, ex-Marathon Digital) is NOT Marathon Petroleum Corporation (NYSE MPC, the Findlay-headquartered refiner and a Hancock County NPDES permittee). Never merge them. The distinction is live in this very record: One Power's S-1 lists "Marathon Petroleum Company LP, Wyandot County, Ohio, 1.5 MW" as a Wind for Industry customer — a different company, a different county, a different contract.

who_is_the_retail_customer.statement: The tariff applies to "the customer," and at this hub it is not established who that is. One Power owns the site and built its own transmission-voltage digital substation; MARA leases capacity behind it under a 15-year take-or-pay lease whose "lease payment is due regardless of whether or not the customer elects to purchase power" (S-1). So the party holding an electric service agreement with AEP Ohio may be One Power rather than MARA, and One Power describes the hub as a multi-tenant "electrified industrial park" for uses spanning fixed and mobile data centers, digital currency mining, electric fleet charging, cathode/anode manufacturing, hydrogen production, indoor farming and additive manufacturing — which is not obviously "used primarily or exclusively for electronic information services." Whether Schedule DCT reaches the hub, reaches its compute tenant, or reaches neither is a question for the ESA, and no ESA, LOA or PUCO filing naming this site was located. Lead HUB-ESA-CUSTOMER.

the_grandfather_question.statement: Two dates set up the question. MARA's 150 MW take-or-pay was announced 2024-11-11 and the hub was energized in 2023 — both before Schedule DCT's Effective Date of 2025-07-23. If an LOA or ESA covering that load was signed before that date, it is "Existing Load," billed at a 60% minimum demand rather than 85%, exempt from the $20,000 supplemental transmission customer charge, and left on its own contract terms. The +300 MW is what breaks it: the tariff makes "Existing Load that signs a new ESA to increase its contract capacity by more than 25,000 kW" into New Load by definition, and +300 MW is twelve times that trigger. On the tariff's own terms an expansion of that size cannot be taken as Existing Load — it is either separately metered New Load, or it converts the whole site. That conclusion follows from the sheets; whether the premise holds (an executed pre-2025-07-23 instrument) is [open] and turns on the ESA nobody has produced.
the_grandfather_question.source: tariff sheets 223-2, 223-3; MARA Holdings release 2024-11-11; One Power Co Form S-1 2025-01-23

behind_the_meter_bearing.statement: The netting provision is the one that reads as if it were written with a site like this one in mind. The hub sits behind One Power's own digital substation, One Power's Hancock County behind-the-meter wind fleet is operating, its Whirlpool Net Zero project in the county is in construction, and AEP has a publicised collaboration to place Bloom fuel cells at data-center customers. Under sheets 223-6/223-7 none of that is free: any non-parallel emergency/backup generation is carved out, but anything designed to operate in parallel needs an interconnection agreement with the Company under O.A.C. 4901:1-22, and electing to net BTM output against Contract Capacity obliges the customer to maintain instantaneous load-curtailment equipment. What the Findlay hub has actually elected is not on any captured record. See behind-the-meter-generation.yaml.

ratepayer_backdrop.statement: AEP's own numbers give the scale the tariff is sorting. Its 2025-09-16 PJM LAS presentation puts the Ohio interconnection queue at 38 GW, DCT study requests at 13.0 GW, and the tariff-adjusted figure at 11.1 GW, with AEP Ohio cumulative summer-peak additions of 2,273 MW by 2026, 7,615 MW by 2030 and 22,272 MW "Ultimate." Its 2026-02-13 release reports 5,642 MW of contracts signed under the DCT as of 2026-02-12 against 12,219 MW signed before it, 17,861 MW total through 2035, from 13,022.7 MW that "asked and paid for a study" and an original ~30,000 MW of requests — against a customer peak demand of roughly 8,000-10,500 MW today.

findlay_share_of_it.statement: None of those figures is broken out by county, substation or customer, and neither document mentions Findlay, Hancock County, One Power or MARA. Findlay's share of the 38 GW queue, the 13.0 GW of study requests, or the 5,642 MW of signed DCT contracts is unknown and must not be estimated.
